messages:
Rae: Noticed a compatibility issue: a fair amount of inbound traffic still uses the 'envelope' POST body (\u007B\"envelope\": {\"payload\": ... }\u007D). Runtime v6 is moving to streamed-chunk-only and expects raw payloads. We need a backward-compat shim strategy at the edge that is low-cost and safe.

Miles: We should avoid heavyweight parsing in the edge path. Header sniffing + small-body heuristic could catch most cases.

Dee: Mobile clients often strip custom headers. Header-only will undercount. In our logs ~18% of old-envelope hits have no X-Client-Version.

Priya: Suggestion: an edge filter that reads only the first N bytes (2KB), tries a resilient JSON probe for "envelope" or "input" keys, and if present, rewrites body to payload. Otherwise pass-through. Add rate caps per tenant to prevent CPU abuse.

Liam: Important: do not attempt on streaming endpoints or chunked-encoding requests. The filter must detect Transfer-Encoding: chunked and bail. Also if Content-Length > 64KB, skip parsing.

Rae: Security & perf checklist: prefix limit 2KB, parse timeout 1ms, per-tenant token bucket for shim path, redact any fields before logging. Also add a global emergency disable toggle.

Miles: Metrics to emit: compat_shim.checks, compat_shim.rewrites, compat_shim.parse_errors, compat_shim.skipped_large_body. Tag by tenant and route. Spike alert if rewrites > 50% of traffic for a tenant in 10m (possible SDK glitch).

Dee: UX: we should expose an opt-in toggle in Console so customers can try the shim before automatic migration. Also email owners when we auto-opt-in after observing sustained success.

Priya: Quick Lua prototype for Envoy (concept):
```lua
function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
  local limit = 2048
  local content_length = tonumber(request_handle:headers():get('content-length') or '0')
  if request_handle:headers():get('transfer-encoding') == 'chunked' or content_length > 65536 then
    return
  end
  local body = request_handle:body():getBytes(0, limit)
  if not body or body == '' then return end
  local ok, obj = pcall(function() return cjson.decode(body) end)
  if ok and obj and obj.envelope and obj.envelope.payload then
    request_handle:body():setBytes(cjson.encode(obj.envelope.payload))
    request_handle:headers():replace('content-length', tostring(#request_handle:body():getBytes(0,-1)))
    request_handle:streamInfo():dynamicMetadata():set('compat','shim','true')
  end
end
```

Liam: We'll need unit tests to simulate partial reads, malformed JSON, and many concurrent small requests. Also run a small canary load to measure CPU tail.

Rae: Rollout plan: 1) canary in staging cluster, 2) opt-in cohort in prod for 48 hours, 3) build auto-opt-in rule: if tenant has >99% rewrite success and low parse_errors for 7 days, we can enable automatically and notify, 4) provide a 60-day deprecation notice and a final off-ramp.

Miles: Ops runbook: steps to disable shim per-region, how to filter traffic for affected tenants, dashboard links, and who to page. I can own the pager rotations for a week after rollout.

Dee: Migration docs: sample code for client authors to stop sending envelope, explain new streaming expectations, and quick SDK patch examples. I'll draft.

ingest-bot: canary deploy initiated: edge/envelope-shim v0.1 -> staging at 1729313000

Rae: Action items recap: Miles - metrics/alerts + canary dashboards; Priya - implement Lua filter with timeouts and config flags; Dee - client migration guide + email template; Liam - tests & perf validation; I'll prepare public deprecation notice draft and coordinate opt-in cohorts.
